newsitem.title: USA: NationsBank eyes West Coast, IPO firms.
newsitem.headline: NationsBank eyes West Coast, IPO firms.

text.p: NationsBank Corp's next big acquisition could involve an initial public offering brokerage firm or a financial institution on the West Coast, according to an interview Chief Executive Hugh McColl gave trade publication Bank Mergers & Acquisitions.

McColl left little doubt that the bank holding company based here would continue to buy banks and other properties, with a goal of generating an earnings mix that is 50 percent fee income and 50 percent interest income, according to published excerpts from the interview.
Bank representatives had no further comment on the story.
"Our long-term goals are to go West. We don't hide that," McColl was quoted as saying.
On the non-bank side, McColl said the company's priority is to buy or align with a brokerage house specializing in initial public offerings.
"Ideally, it would be a house inside of our region," McColl was quoted as saying. He said IPO capability would generate long-term customers for the bank.

"We get an entrepreneur up to a certain place and then he wants to go public. If we can't take him to the common stock market, then somebody like Goldman, Sachs is his buddy, not us. And if we take him to the market, he gets rich, he puts his money in our investment-managed fund. I've got a cradle-to-grave customer."
McColl declined to speculate about possible targets.
In the interview, he also says the cornerstone of the bank's acquisition strategy is to build leading market share in fast-growing territories adjacent to or in markets already served by NationsBank.
Shares of NationsBank were off 1/4 to 105-3/4.
